problem: Large pretrained VLN models (DUET, ScaleVLN, ~181M params) are too heavy for resource-constrained embodied platforms. Prior distillation work distills only in pre-training (PR-KD) or only in fine-tuning (MAGIC), leaving a large gap to the teacher.
motivation: Embodied agents need real-time on-device inference, but the best VLN models are computationally expensive. VLN training has two phases that learn different things (fine-grained feature/alignment knowledge vs navigation decision knowledge), so distilling in both should transfer more.
key_idea: A progressive two-stage knowledge distillation: layer-wise attention and hidden-state distillation in pre-training, then text, panorama and fused-logit distillation in fine-tuning, giving a DUET-style student with ~12% of the teacher's parameters.
insight: The two stages are complementary. On REVERIE val-unseen, dropping both distillation stages gives SR 49.16 / SPL 36.96, pretrain-only KD gives 54.13 / 38.64, finetune-only KD gives 52.60 / 41.77, and both give 54.30 / 42.02. Among the fine-tuning losses, distilling the fused local-global logits matters most (removing it drops R2R val-unseen SR from 78.80 to 75.01). The KD weight of 0.1 is best.
method: Student architecture: DUET-style dual-scale graph transformer shrunk to N_L=3 language, N_P=1 panorama and N_X=2 cross-modal blocks (teacher 9/2/4), ~21.95M params.

Pre-training distillation: MSE on instruction embeddings (learnable projection W_e), plus per-block attention-matrix MSE and hidden-state MSE (with projection W_h). Student block m maps to teacher block h(m)=3m for the language encoder and 2m for the panorama and cross-modal encoders.
Fine-tuning text-encoder distillation: MSE between teacher and student instruction features (L_txt, with projection W_l).
Fine-tuning panorama distillation: MSE between teacher and student panoramic features (L_pano, with projection W_r).
Fused-logit distillation: cross-entropy between the teacher's and student's fused local-global action logits (L_fuse, temperature t=1).
Total fine-tuning loss: the original action loss plus 0.1 × (L_txt + L_pano + L_fuse).
Teachers: ScaleVLN (pretrained and fine-tuned checkpoints) on R2R and AutoVLN on REVERIE. Training is 200k iterations at batch size 16 on R2R and 20k iterations at batch size 32 on REVERIE.

setting.backbone: MiniVLN: small DUET-style dual-scale graph transformer student (fine-tuned via distillation from ScaleVLN / AutoVLN teachers)
setting.training_data: R2R (with ScaleVLN's augmented data via the teacher) and REVERIE (AutoVLN teacher); pre-training and fine-tuning with distillation from the teachers
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views per viewpoint, ViT features) with topological map
setting.privileged: none at test time (teacher is used only in training); the teacher model's features are used during distillation

numbers.evidence: Table 1 (Comparison with SoTA on R2R): MiniVLN 78.80 / 70.17

numbers_note: The non-distilled baseline numbers for R2R (SR 74.16 / SPL 65.15 val unseen; 73.59 / 63.78 test) are given only in the text and a figure. CPU inference speed results are shown only in a figure.
results: MiniVLN, with 21.95M parameters (~12% of the teacher), reaches R2R test-unseen SR 77.59 / SPL 68.05, on par with or above ScaleVLN (77 / 68), and beats the MAGIC-M/S distilled students. On REVERIE it slightly exceeds the AutoVLN teacher on SPL and RGSPL and gets ~97% of its SR and RGS. On CPU inference it is over 3x faster than the teacher.
limitations: Only evaluated in the Matterport3D simulator, on R2R and REVERIE, with a DUET-style architecture; no real-robot or on-device (edge hardware) test, only a laptop CPU speed simulation.
Still needs a large teacher and full two-stage training; the distilled model is not the smallest (MAGIC-S has fewer params, 11.14M), and REVERIE SR/RGS remain below the teacher.
Speed results are only in a figure, and teacher-student layer mapping is hand-designed.
